hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Mayor's Race and Trash Pickup Question Head to Voters
hero.teaser: Incumbent Mayor Shannon Martin faces challenger Steven Giordano as early voting continues, while a non-binding ballot question asks residents whether the city should switch to twice-a-week trash collection.
hero.body:
Early voting is underway in Port St. Lucie's mayoral election, pitting incumbent Shannon Martin against challenger Steven Giordano, with the election less than two weeks away. Voters are also weighing in on a non-binding ballot question asking whether the city should move to twice-a-week trash pickup.

 On the first day of early voting, campaign tents for both mayoral candidates stood side by side at a polling location on Rosser Blvd. Martin is running to keep her seat and says the city should stay on its current course, pointing to infrastructure work such as roadwork as a reason voters should keep her in City Hall. Giordano says City Hall has become corrupt and lost touch with everyday residents.

 When asked what he would do differently, he also focused on roadwork, saying the city needs a new traffic study. Port St. Lucie's mayor serves a four-year term and holds significant influence under the city's mayor-council form of government. Candidates for mayor do not run with party affiliation.

 Trash collection has also become a flashpoint in the city, which contracts with FCC for garbage service. At recent city council meetings, residents have criticized the quality of pickup and demanded an additional collection day each week. But on the first day of early voting, people interviewed at the polls said they would rather keep the current schedule. Resident Rob Buske summed up that sentiment, saying, "I don't want to pay for something I don't need." A second weekly pickup day would cost residents more than $100 a year.

 The ballot question on trash service is non-binding, meaning it serves only as a poll of resident opinion. City council members are not required to act on the results regardless of how residents vote. Like the mayoral race, the trash question carries no party affiliation, leaving voters to settle both the city's leadership and its collection schedule on the same ballot.

cards.headline: Red Flag Warnings, 4-6 Foot Surf Keep St. Lucie Beaches on High Hazard Alert
cards.teaser: Dangerous surf and rip current risk are prompting St. Lucie County Ocean Rescue to urge swimmers toward lifeguarded beaches like Pepper Park and Waveland Beach.
cards.body:
A red flag warning was in effect this week at Fort Pierce Inlet State Park and other St. Lucie County beaches, where waves between four and six feet crashed along the shoreline Wednesday. The high hazard conditions are tied to a low pressure system sitting off the eastern U.S. coast in the mid-Atlantic.

 St. Lucie County Ocean Rescue says the rough surf makes it more important than ever for swimmers to stick to lifeguarded beaches, pointing specifically to Pepper Park and Waveland Beach. Officials say both locations will likely be flying red or double red flags over the next few days as the hazardous conditions continue.

 The county warns that rip currents are possible in these conditions. Ocean Rescue advises anyone caught in a rip current not to panic and to swim parallel to the shoreline until free of the current.

 The choppy water has still drawn surfers into the waves. Foil surfer Lisa Rose described the challenge of the conditions. "It was very windy and very choppy and it's really challenging because you have to negotiate all of the chop," she said.

 Surfer Jodi Riley said she only went in as far as her waist. "I went in, not with my surfboard, but like, to my waist and it's just, it's rough and it's just not super safe for like, I'm sort of a beginner so not safe for me, but like, some of the other surfers have definitely been out," Riley said. Fort Pierce resident Lee Bertucelli also ventured into the water but kept his distance from the deeper surf.

 "I went in, you know, not too far. The waves were fun, but again not too far, didn't want to deal with rip tides or anything else," Bertucelli said. Describing the sea itself, Bertucelli added, "The sea was angry today my friends."

cards.teaser: A 60-year-old Vero Beach man died Thursday after the SUV he was driving collided with a semi-trailer at the intersection of 66th Avenue and 49th Street in Indian River County. Acco
cards.body:
A 60-year-old Vero Beach man died Thursday after the SUV he was driving collided with a semi-trailer at the intersection of 66th Avenue and 49th Street in Indian River County. According to a Florida Highway Patrol crash report, a 2026 Freightliner truck-tractor pulling a flatbed trailer was turning left from a stop sign on westbound 49th Street when it entered the path of a northbound 2006 Dodge Durango traveling on 66th Avenue. The front of the Durango struck the left side of the trailer.

 The Durango driver was taken to Health First's Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he was pronounced dead at 8:02 a.m. His next of kin had not been notified, according to the report.

 The 59-year-old Jacksonville man driving the Freightliner reported no injuries.

cards.body:
For the Packard family, roofing has never been simply a business passed from one generation to the next. It has been a trade learned firsthand, a family responsibility and, over time, a connection to the communities the company serves.

 Packard Roofing & Waterproofing has grown from a South Florida roofing company into a multigenerational operation serving homeowners across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

 The Port St. Lucie family business was founded in Miami in 1971 by Raymond M. Packard and David R. Packard. More than two decades later, the company expanded to Port St. Lucie in 1994, establishing the Treasure Coast operation that now serves customers across Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties.

 Today, the company is led by third-generation siblings Brian Packard and Stephanie Packard Smith.

 Brian's path into the family business started well before he was old enough to run one. As a teenager, he spent summers cleaning and organizing the warehouse and service yard. Later came tear-off crews, repair work, and eventually handling residential and commercial projects himself.

 Stephanie's history with the company also stretches back decades. She joined during the hectic aftermath of Hurricane Andrew in 1992, when South Florida roofing companies were dealing with enormous demand while Packard Roofing was also recovering from storm damage to its own facilities. She went on to become a central part of the company's office operations.

 Brian relocated from Miami to Port St. Lucie in 2021 as the family prepared for another transition. Following their father David Packard's death in 2022, Brian and Stephanie took responsibility for leading the company into its third generation.

 A business built around the Treasure Coast

 Packard Roofing's headquarters at 2182 NW Reserve Park Trace places the company beside PGA Village in Port St. Lucie, with much of its work concentrated throughout the Treasure Coast.

 The company handles roof repairs, roof replacements, new roof construction, and maintenance for homeowners throughout Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties.

 That local focus matters in a region where roofs face intense sun, heavy rainfall, tropical weather, and wind-driven rain. For homeowners, problems can range from persistent leaks and storm damage to aging roofs that have reached the end of their useful lifespan.

 Packard Roofing's website also provides homeowners with information about issues such as hurricane preparation, wind damage, roof leaks, and deciding when a roof should be repaired rather than replaced.

 For a company with decades behind it, that focus reflects an effort to remain useful to homeowners before they ever need a major roofing project.

 Experience that stayed with the company

 The Packard family is not the only long-term presence in the business.

 Superintendent Mark Hanna has worked with the company for more than 30 years, beginning as a repairman before moving into a leadership role overseeing repair and replacement work. His responsibilities now include supervising projects, preparing estimates, and often serving as one of the first people customers meet when they contact the company.

 That kind of employee longevity fits the broader story of a company that has transitioned across three generations without abandoning its family-business identity.

 Packard's philosophy, according to the family, has remained centered on straightforward communication, quality materials, and workmanship the company is willing to stand behind. The company says many customers return when they move to another home or recommend Packard to younger generations of their own families.

 Looking toward another generation

 More than five decades after the company was founded, Packard Roofing is operating in a Treasure Coast that looks very different from the one it entered in the 1990s.

 Port St. Lucie has grown around it. PGA Village and surrounding communities have expanded. New homes continue to rise while existing roofs move through the repair and replacement cycle that comes with age and Florida weather.

 The business has changed with that growth, but its leadership still describes Packard in distinctly family terms.

 For Brian, continuing the company means carrying forward standards established by his grandfather and father rather than simply preserving a business name. He has described honesty, hard work and quality craftsmanship as values passed down through three generations.

 Packard Roofing & Waterproofing provides roof repair, replacement, maintenance, and new-roof construction throughout Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties.

 Local leaders, community partners and Xfinity team members gathered on October 21 for a ribbon-cutting ceremony at the new Stuart Xfinity Store. hero.headline: Red Flag Warnings, 4-6 Foot Surf Keep St. Lucie Beaches on High Hazard Alert
hero.teaser: Dangerous surf and rip current risk are prompting St. Lucie County Ocean Rescue to urge swimmers toward lifeguarded beaches like Pepper Park and Waveland Beach.
hero.body:
A red flag warning was in effect this week at Fort Pierce Inlet State Park and other St. Lucie County beaches, where waves between four and six feet crashed along the shoreline Wednesday. The high hazard conditions are tied to a low pressure system sitting off the eastern U.S. coast in the mid-Atlantic.

 St. Lucie County Ocean Rescue says the rough surf makes it more important than ever for swimmers to stick to lifeguarded beaches, pointing specifically to Pepper Park and Waveland Beach. Officials say both locations will likely be flying red or double red flags over the next few days as the hazardous conditions continue.

 The county warns that rip currents are possible in these conditions. Ocean Rescue advises anyone caught in a rip current not to panic and to swim parallel to the shoreline until free of the current.

 The choppy water has still drawn surfers into the waves. Foil surfer Lisa Rose described the challenge of the conditions. "It was very windy and very choppy and it's really challenging because you have to negotiate all of the chop," she said.

 Surfer Jodi Riley said she only went in as far as her waist. "I went in, not with my surfboard, but like, to my waist and it's just, it's rough and it's just not super safe for like, I'm sort of a beginner so not safe for me, but like, some of the other surfers have definitely been out," Riley said. Fort Pierce resident Lee Bertucelli also ventured into the water but kept his distance from the deeper surf.

 "I went in, you know, not too far. The waves were fun, but again not too far, didn't want to deal with rip tides or anything else," Bertucelli said. Describing the sea itself, Bertucelli added, "The sea was angry today my friends."

cards.headline: Xfinity Celebrates New Store in Stuart
cards.teaser: Comcast celebrates the opening of a new Xfinity Store in Stuart and announces a $35,000 grant supporting Martin County PAL’s Rising Responders program.
cards.body:
*New location offers convenient access to Xfinity and Comcast Business products and services*

 Stuart, FL – October 21, 2026 – Comcast is celebrating the grand opening of its newest Xfinity Store in Stuart. Located at 3955 Southeast Federal Highway, Stuart, FL 34997, the store features an interactive, modern design that gives residents the opportunity to explore the full suite of Xfinity products and services. Local business leaders can also visit the store to discuss their technology needs with a Comcast Business expert.

 “Opening this new Xfinity Store reflects how important it is to give customers a welcoming, convenient place to learn about Xfinity services,” said Jackie Guerry Maybeck, Vice President of Sales & Marketing for Comcast’s Florida Region . “We look forward to serving the Stuart community and helping residents and businesses explore fast, reliable Xfinity Internet with powerful WiFi, Xfinity Mobile, and entertainment solutions that work best for them.”

 Local leaders, community partners and Xfinity team members gathered on October 21 for a ribbon-cutting ceremony at the new Stuart Xfinity Store. The event featured remarks from Jackie Guerry Maybeck, Vice President of Sales & Marketing for Comcast’s Florida Region; Ed Ciampi, Martin County Commissioner; Ted Astolfi, CEO of the Economic Council of Martin County; Troy McDonald, Interim Executive Director of the Business Development Board of Martin County; and Noel DelValle, Executive Director at Martin County PAL.

 “Stuart and communities across Martin County value strong connections and convenient access to the services people rely on every day,” said Edward V. Ciampi, Martin County Commissioner . “This new Xfinity Store gives our constituents and local businesses another place to get hands-on support and find technology that meets their changing needs.”

 The opening also drew support from Martin County’s business community, whose leaders highlighted what the new location represents for the area’s continued growth.

 “The opening of Xfinity’s store in Stuart is a meaningful investment in Martin County, and a strong reflection of the confidence businesses continue to place in our community,” said Ted Astolfi, CEO of the Economic Council of Martin County . “A strong local economy depends on giving people and businesses the tools to move ideas forward, and this new location creates a place where customers can explore new technology and find solutions that fit the way they live and work.”

 “Stuart continues to grow as a place where families can thrive and businesses can build for the future, and investments that bring new services and resources to our community help support that momentum,” said Troy McDonald, Interim Executive Director of the Business Development Board of Martin County . “We appreciate Comcast’s continued commitment to the area and look forward to seeing this new Xfinity Store become a valuable resource for residents, local businesses and families across our community.”

 The new storefront expands Xfinity’s retail footprint in the Sunshine State, following recent store opening in Doral , Jacksonville , Fort Myers , Delray Beach , Fort Lauderdale , Kendall , Miami Gardens , Naples , North Miami , and Tallahassee . It also strengthens Xfinity’s presence in the Treasure Coast with three additional Xfinity Stores located nearby:

 Stuart (Jensen Plaza) - 2830 NW Federal Highway, Stuart, FL 34994 Port St. Lucie - 277 SW Port St Lucie Blvd, Port St. Lucie, FL 34984 Vero Beach - 5840 20th Street, Vero Beach, FL 32966 During the grand opening, Comcast announced a $35,000 grant to Martin County PAL to support its Rising Responders: Digital Pathways to Emergency Medical Careers program. The initiative will equip 12 underserved middle and high school students with the technology, digital literacy and workforce skills needed to pursue careers in emergency medical services and healthcare.

 The grant will also provide broadband training and digital navigation services to PAL families and community members, reaching an estimated 200 people annually through workshops and one-on-one support. The investment is part of Project UP, Comcast’s $1 billion commitment to advancing digital opportunity and building a future of unlimited possibilities.

 “This investment will give young people access to the technology, training and practical skills they need to explore careers in emergency medical services and healthcare,” said Noel DelValle, Executive Director at Martin County PAL . “It will also expand critical digital literacy resources and one-on-one support to families across our community, extending the impact well beyond the students in the program.”

 Store employees are ready to welcome customers into the new retail space, where visitors can explore the latest Xfinity Internet, Mobile, TV and smart home technologies, see products in action and receive personalized support from on-site specialists.

 Explore Innovative Products 

 Xfinity Internet : Learn about multi-gigabit Internet speeds, powerful WiFi that reaches every corner of the home and super-responsive connections with low lag, all to power streaming, gaming, videoconferencing, and more – all available with a five-year price guarantee. Xfinity Mobile and Comcast Business Mobile : Purchase new mobile phones, devices, and accessories, and get exclusive access to speeds of up to 1 gigabit per second with WiFi PowerBoost when connected to millions of Xfinity WiFi hotspots across the country – regardless of home Internet speed. Customers can get the first line of Xfinity Mobile included for a year with qualifying Xfinity Internet plans. Xfinity TV : Xfinity brings together live TV, streaming, sports, and on-demand content in one easy-to-use experience. With the award-winning Xfinity Voice Remote, finding a show, channel, or game is fast, easy, and frustration-free. Xfinity Home Solutions : Help protect what matters most with solutions ranging from WiFi Shield , included with eligible Xfinity Internet service, to Shield Select for self-monitored home protection, and Xfinity Home Security for professionally-monitored security. Comcast Business : Connect with a subject-matter expert to discuss Comcast Business’ full suite of solutions, including fast, reliable connectivity, secure networking solutions, advanced cybersecurity, and a range of managed service options to meet the needs of businesses of all sizes. Connect to the Nation’s Most Reliable WiFi Day One 

 New customers now have the option to choose same-day pick up at this local Xfinity store or, if available, same-day Gateway delivery to their home. And, even before the Gateway arrives, customers have immediate access to Xfinity’s network of more than 23 million secure WiFi hotspots the moment they sign up.

 Engage with a Local, Dedicated Team of Experts 

 Xfinity Stores are staffed with highly trained, knowledgeable sales consultants who can walk customers through product demonstrations, help them sign up for services, learn more about their current services or devices, review accounts, manage equipment, and more.

 Visitors can drop in and explore the store instead of waiting in line with a time-saving queuing system, or go online to https://www.xfinity.com/support/contact-us , click “Find one near you” and make an appointment.

 The new Stuart Xfinity Store is open Monday through Saturday from 9 a.m. – 8 p.m., and Sunday from 10 a.m. – 6 p.m. For directions and store hours, click here .

cards.headline: Vero Beach Man, 60, Dies in Crash With Semi at 66th and 49th
cards.teaser: A 60-year-old Vero Beach man died Thursday after the SUV he was driving collided with a semi-trailer at the intersection of 66th Avenue and 49th Street in Indian River County. Acco
cards.body:
A 60-year-old Vero Beach man died Thursday after the SUV he was driving collided with a semi-trailer at the intersection of 66th Avenue and 49th Street in Indian River County. According to a Florida Highway Patrol crash report, a 2026 Freightliner truck-tractor pulling a flatbed trailer was turning left from a stop sign on westbound 49th Street when it entered the path of a northbound 2006 Dodge Durango traveling on 66th Avenue. The front of the Durango struck the left side of the trailer.

 The Durango driver was taken to Health First's Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he was pronounced dead at 8:02 a.m. His next of kin had not been notified, according to the report.

 The 59-year-old Jacksonville man driving the Freightliner reported no injuries.
